access.notes: CANOPUS is accessed through SIRIUS web services and is currently free for academic use under the SIRIUS licensing terms.

Summarize chemical diversity across large untargeted metabolomics datasets at class level.
Provide structural context for features absent from spectral and molecular-structure reference databases.

designed_for: Compound-class prediction from accurate-mass tandem mass spectra.
requirements: SIRIUS-compatible high-resolution MS/MS data and access to the SIRIUS webservice.
considerations: CANOPUS predicts compound classes rather than exact structures; results should not be reported as compound-level identifications.

strategies.summary: A transferable natural-product discovery strategy that overlays quantitative bioassay results onto LC-MS feature abundance and MS/MS molecular networks to prioritize molecular families and individual features associated with biological activity.
strategies.description: Bioactivity-Based Molecular Networking adds an orthogonal biological evidence layer to molecular networking. Fractionated samples are profiled by LC-MS/MS and tested in a quantitative bioassay. Feature abundances across fractions are correlated with bioactivity, producing a bioactivity score that is mapped onto the molecular network. This allows active molecular families and candidate analogues to be prioritized before isolation while preserving molecular-network annotation and dereplication context.

strategies.name: Chemoselective reactivity-resolved metabolomics
strategies.summary: A functional-group-resolved metabolomics strategy that uses orthogonal chemoselective probes, covalent capture and diagnostic reporter chemistry to enrich and organize otherwise chemically heterogeneous metabolite subsets before LC-MS.
strategies.description: The modular reactivity-encoding platform (MREP) uses distinct alkyne-tagged probes for carboxyl, amine, carbonyl and thiol functionalities. Tagged metabolites are captured through click chemistry on a common resin, matrix is removed, and released derivatives share reporter-ion behavior. The strategy converts intrinsic chemical reactivity into an experimental annotation/enrichment dimension.

strategies.name: Credentialing untargeted metabolomics features
strategies.summary: A method-development strategy that uses mixtures of natural-abundance and uniformly 13C-labeled biological extracts to distinguish genuine biological features from artifacts and benchmark untargeted metabolomics workflows.
strategies.description: Credentialing creates an experimental ground truth for whether untargeted LC-MS features arise from biological metabolites. Natural-abundance and uniformly 13C-labeled material are mixed at defined ratios; expected isotope spacing and intensity relationships are used to label credible biological features. The number and quality of credentialed features can then be used to optimize extraction, chromatography, acquisition or feature-processing parameters.

strategies.name: DDA-assisted DIA metabolomics
strategies.summary: A hybrid untargeted acquisition strategy that analyzes individual samples by DIA for broad feature and MS/MS coverage while using pooled quality-control samples by DDA to obtain cleaner fragmentation spectra for annotation.
strategies.description: DaDIA deliberately separates the strengths of two acquisition modes across the study design. Biological samples are acquired using data-independent acquisition to maximize feature and fragmentation coverage, while pooled QC samples are acquired using data-dependent acquisition to generate higher-quality, less multiplexed MS/MS spectra. Computational integration then associates the complementary DDA and DIA evidence for metabolite annotation.

strategies.name: Suspect screening of exposome-related xenobiotics
strategies.summary: An exposomics strategy that interrogates untargeted UHPLC-HRMS/MS data with curated lists of plausible xenobiotics and metabolites, then applies chromatographic, spectral, and error-control evidence to prioritize candidate exposures.

Rather than requiring authentic standards for every analyte or searching every detected feature without prior hypotheses, the workflow begins with curated suspect lists and tests whether those candidates are supported by accurate mass, chromatographic peak quality, fragmentation evidence, and matrix-aware filtering. The 2024 workflow evaluated this approach across multiple human biofluids and explicitly measured false-positive and false-negative behavior.

strategies.name: Ion Identity Molecular Networking (IIMN)
strategies.summary: A strategy extending feature-based molecular networking with MS1-derived ion relationships, linking candidate ion species of the same molecule alongside MS/MS spectral-similarity edges.
strategies.description: Ion Identity Molecular Networking adds a second evidence layer to an FBMN network: relationships between candidate adducts, multimers and other ion species supported by chromatographic behavior and mass differences. MS1 ion-identity edges and MS/MS similarity edges have different meanings and should be interpreted separately. The published GNPS implementation can also collapse ion groups for visualization. These groupings are hypotheses about ion origin, not proof of a molecular structure.

strategies.name: Colony-based MALDI-MS/MS dereplication with IDBac and GNPS2

Protein and specialized-metabolite MS1 data are first used to understand isolate identity and metabolite-production potential. Selected precursor ions are then fragmented by MALDI-MS/MS, and the resulting spectra are passed to GNPS2 for molecular networking and library searching. The layered workflow adds preliminary structural context early enough to influence which strains are advanced to scale-up.

strategies.summary: A microbial natural-product discovery strategy that combines MALDI protein fingerprinting with specialized-metabolite overlap to reduce taxonomic and chemical redundancy when constructing or downsizing isolate libraries.
strategies.description: This strategy uses two complementary MALDI information spaces before scale-up. Protein-region spectra group bacterial isolates by taxonomic or strain-level similarity, while lower-mass specialized-metabolite spectra reveal chemical overlap within those groups. Isolates can then be selected to preserve phylogenetic breadth while minimizing redundant natural-product profiles, shifting strain prioritization from morphology or taxonomy alone to combined biological and chemical evidence.

strategies.name: Metabologenomics
strategies.summary: A natural-product discovery strategy that correlates metabolite occurrence across a strain collection with biosynthetic gene-cluster or gene-cluster-family occurrence to connect chemistry with its likely genetic origin.

Predicted distributions remain model outputs, not additional MS measurements or evidence of molecular identification.

Navigator review checked publication identity and methodological scope; linked software was not independently benchmarked.

publication.title: Integration of mass cytometry and mass spectrometry imaging for spatially resolved single-cell metabolic profiling

strategies.name: Native MS metabolomics for metal-binding compounds
strategies.summary: A transferable LC-MS strategy that combines post-column pH adjustment and metal infusion with ion identity molecular networking to discover small molecules that bind metals in complex biological samples.
strategies.description: This strategy adapts native electrospray concepts to metabolomics so that protonated and metal-bound forms of the same chromatographic analyte can be detected together. Post-column pH adjustment and infusion of a selected metal are coupled to feature processing and ion identity molecular networking, allowing candidate metal-binding molecules to be prioritized from characteristic mass offsets and shared chromatographic behavior.

strategies.name: Ozone-induced dissociation for structural lipidomics
strategies.summary: A structural-lipidomics strategy that uses ozone-induced dissociation to generate diagnostic fragments for carbon–carbon double-bond positions that conventional CID-based lipidomics often cannot resolve.
strategies.description: Ozone-induced dissociation (OzID) adds gas-phase chemical reactivity to lipid analysis. Reactions of mass-selected unsaturated lipid ions produce diagnostic fragments that locate carbon–carbon double bonds. The method complements collision-induced fragmentation. Later implementations can combine separation and automated interpretation, but their acquisition and software requirements are implementation-specific.

strategies.name: Reverse metabolomics
strategies.summary: A discovery strategy that starts from a candidate chemical structure or reference MS/MS spectrum, searches public metabolomics repositories for matching spectra, and uses sample metadata to reveal biological or phenotypic associations.
strategies.description: Reverse metabolomics reverses the usual untargeted workflow. Instead of starting with an unknown feature and attempting to infer its structure, the researcher begins with a candidate structure and an experimental MS/MS spectrum, searches public metabolomics data for matching spectra, and then uses repository metadata to ask where the molecule occurs. The resulting organism, biospecimen, phenotype or disease associations can guide biological validation.

publication.title: Reverse metabolomics for the discovery of chemical structures from humans
publication.citation: Gentry EC, Collins SL, Panitchpakdi M, et al. Reverse metabolomics for the discovery of chemical structures from humans. Nature 626, 419–426 (2024).

workflow_steps.description: Use the reference spectrum as a query against public metabolomics datasets to identify files and datasets containing related spectra.

workflow_steps.title: Contextualize matches with sample metadata
workflow_steps.description: Summarize organism, biospecimen, phenotype, disease state and other standardized metadata associated with matching public files.

workflow_steps.title: Prioritize biological associations
workflow_steps.description: Use the distribution of matched spectra across public datasets to generate hypotheses about where the molecule occurs and which phenotypes or sample types it may be associated with.

workflow_steps.title: Validate prioritized associations
workflow_steps.description: Test the proposed association in independent cohorts, targeted measurements, culture systems, or functional experiments appropriate to the biological question.

strategies.name: Spatially registered single-cell metabolomics
strategies.summary: A single-cell metabolomics strategy that registers microscopy-derived cell boundaries and morphologic information with MALDI imaging mass spectrometry so spatial ion signals can be assigned to individual cells.
strategies.description: SpaceM combines light microscopy, image segmentation, MALDI mass spectrometry imaging, and spatial registration to convert tissue- or culture-level ion images into per-cell metabolic profiles. The key methodological step is aligning optical cell information with MSI ablation coordinates so metabolite signals can be associated with individual cells while retaining morpho-spatial context.

publication.title: SpaceM reveals metabolic states of single cells
publication.citation: Rappez L, Stadler M, Triana S, et al. SpaceM reveals metabolic states of single cells. Nature Methods 18, 799-805 (2021).

workflow_steps.description: Collect spatially resolved metabolite signals across the same cellular field.

workflow_steps.description: Align cell masks with MALDI ablation locations so mass-spectral signals can be assigned to individual cells.

workflow_steps.title: Construct per-cell metabolic profiles
workflow_steps.description: Aggregate registered ion signals into a cell-by-metabolite matrix while retaining morphologic and spatial information.

considerations: Cell-level profiles depend on segmentation and registration accuracy.

strategies.name: Stable-isotope labeling–assisted molecular networking
strategies.summary: A biosynthetic discovery strategy that combines stable-isotope precursor feeding with LC-MS/MS molecular networking to identify structurally related metabolites that incorporate a defined biosynthetic building block.
strategies.description: Stable-isotope labeling–assisted molecular networking layers biosynthetic incorporation information onto MS/MS similarity. A labeled precursor such as a stable-isotope amino acid is supplied to a producing organism, labeled mass shifts are detected in metabolite features, and molecular networking groups related MS/MS spectra. The combination helps distinguish biosynthetically connected analogues and can provide sequence or building-block information that molecular networking alone does not supply.

publication.title: Combining Stable Isotope Labeling and Molecular Networking for Biosynthetic Pathway Characterization
publication.citation: Klitgaard A, Nielsen JB, Frandsen RJN, Andersen MR, Nielsen KF. Combining Stable Isotope Labeling and Molecular Networking for Biosynthetic Pathway Characterization. Analytical Chemistry 87, 6520–6526 (2015).

workflow_steps.title: Select and feed a stable-isotope precursor
workflow_steps.description: Add a labeled biosynthetic building block to the culture under conditions that permit incorporation into specialized metabolites, while retaining appropriate unlabeled controls.

workflow_steps.title: Detect isotope incorporation
workflow_steps.description: Compare labeled and unlabeled LC-MS data to identify features with mass shifts consistent with incorporation of the supplied precursor.

workflow_steps.title: Acquire and compare MS/MS spectra
workflow_steps.description: Collect fragmentation spectra for candidate labeled and related metabolites.

workflow_steps.title: Build a molecular network
workflow_steps.description: Organize structurally related spectra by MS/MS similarity and overlay isotope-incorporation evidence to recognize families sharing the labeled building block.

workflow_steps.title: Infer biosynthetic or structural relationships
workflow_steps.description: Use the combined label pattern and fragmentation relationships to prioritize analogues, infer building-block composition, and guide targeted structural validation.

tools.role: Molecular networking of related MS/MS spectra.

Characterizing families of peptide or other metabolites where isotope incorporation provides interpretable biosynthetic information.
requirements: A biologically plausible labeled precursor and culture system capable of incorporating it.
Matched labeled and unlabeled controls and sufficient mass accuracy to resolve the expected isotope shift.
considerations: Label incorporation may be incomplete, diluted by metabolism, or redistributed into downstream metabolites.
Molecular similarity and label incorporation support a biosynthetic relationship but do not by themselves establish complete pathway genetics or final structure.

provenance.notes: Included as an Analytical Strategy because stable-isotope incorporation adds a biosynthetic evidence layer to molecular-network relationships and is transferable beyond the original fungal system. Navigator review checked publication identity and methodological scope; linked software was not independently benchmarked.

strategies.name: Taxonomically informed metabolite annotation
strategies.summary: A metabolite-annotation strategy that reranks candidate natural-product structures by combining spectral or in-silico annotation evidence with the taxonomic distance between the study organism and known producers of candidate compounds.
strategies.description: Taxonomically informed scoring adds biological provenance to conventional candidate ranking. Candidate structures are first generated from spectral libraries or in-silico annotation. Known organism–compound associations are then used to calculate taxonomic relevance, allowing candidates reported from related organisms to receive additional support without treating taxonomy as structural proof.

workflow_steps.description: Combine chemical and taxonomic evidence while retaining the original annotation evidence and uncertainty.

Candidate structures with linked biological-source metadata.
considerations: Taxonomy is supporting evidence and cannot establish structure.
Published occurrence databases are incomplete and biased toward studied taxa.
The linked contemporary resources illustrate ways to implement the strategy; they are not all software used in the original publication.

provenance.notes: Included because taxonomy is an independent biological evidence layer added to conventional chemical annotation. Navigator review checked publication identity and methodological scope; linked software was not independently benchmarked.

strategies.name: 3D molecular cartography
strategies.summary: A spatial metabolomics strategy that combines systematic surface sampling, LC-MS/MS, coordinate-aware metadata and 2D/3D molecular mapping to reconstruct the distribution of metabolites and environmental chemicals across physical objects.
strategies.description: 3D molecular cartography extends metabolomics beyond conventional bulk samples by attaching each extraction to a physical coordinate. LC-MS data are processed and annotated, then mapped onto photographs or 3D surface models so chemical distributions can be explored spatially. Cartographical snapshots preserve visualization settings for reproducibility.

Observed distributions integrate extraction, LC-MS detectability and sampling effects.
